utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, it’s coming along nicely—folks have been dropping off tools and supplies all morning. If you’re thinking of helping, I can point you to where they still need hands.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: So it’s really still going on today, right? If you need confirmation, I can help with whatever’s still short.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh yes, still going strong today—there’s plenty left to do, especially sorting supplies and hauling boxes. If you can pitch in, I’d be grateful!

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: I’ll mention the repair drive to the others and make sure the plan gets around.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Thanks, Vik — I appreciate that. I’ll try to keep up this time.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Of course — I’ll spread the word and keep everyone in the loop.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: I can help with the repair drive—what do you need me to bring?

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Thanks, Leo — could you bring a screwdriver set, some gloves, and a roll of duct tape?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Got it — I’ll bring those.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I can help where I can—what kind of repairs are we gathering for?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Mostly basics—tools, patch kits, nails, and a few spare parts would really help.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Got it — I can bring some nails and a few spare parts. If you want, I can also ask around for tools.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I can help coordinate around the school schedule for the repair drive—what time are you thinking?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: That would be amazing—thank you. I was thinking late afternoon, maybe around 4:30, so it doesn’t clash with pickup time.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: 4:30 sounds like a good fit—I can help spread the word and keep it clear of pickup chaos.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: I’d like to keep this simple: let’s pick a time, make a short list, and stick to it.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: That sounds good to me, Eli. I’ll keep it simple and write the list down so I don’t forget.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Good, Oren—let’s do Saturday morning for a quick look and list the main fixes.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Oh, Pia, you should come by the repair drive—we’ve got folks helping with all sorts of fixes, and it’d be great to see you there!

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I might stop by, but I need to check the timing and whether I can bring the right stuff.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Totally, just swing by whenever you can—there’ll be people around to point you to what’s needed. If you want, I can send you the timing and a quick list of stuff to bring.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Oh, I heard a little about the repair drive—how’s it going so far?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: It’s coming along nicely, Nell—people have been generous and the sign-up sheet is filling up. I’m just lining up a few more volunteers and supplies so we can get everything fixed up smoothly.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: That’s great to hear, Rosa—glad folks are pitching in. Let me know if you need another pair of hands or a quick update pass along.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Before I help, can you tell me what needs repairing and when the drive starts?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: It’s mostly small household fixes like leaky taps, loose door handles, and a few broken shelves, and the repair drive starts this Saturday morning at the community hall.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks—that helps. I’ll note the taps, handles, and shelves, and get there Saturday morning at the community hall.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I can help if you still need me—I’m just keeping things low-key today.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Appreciate it, Uli — I’ll probably swing by a bit late, but I may still need a hand once I get there.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: That’s fine, Dane — just let me know when you arrive. I’ll be around.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Sure thing, Mina — I’ve got a few tools I can lend for the repair drive. Just let me know what you need.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Great, Gus — do you have a wrench set and a power drill I could borrow?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Yep, I’ve got both you can borrow. I’ll set them aside for you—just swing by when you’re ready.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I’m keeping an eye on where the repair drive is set up and can point you there if you need it.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Thanks, Opal — just point me over when you get a chance.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Sure thing — it’s over by the community center parking lot. Just head past the library, and I’ll guide you the rest of the way.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Sure thing — I can lend a hand with tools for the repair drive if you need them.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Thanks, Gus — I appreciate that. I’ll keep you in mind if we’re short on tools.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: No problem at all — just give me a shout if you end up needing anything.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I’m happy to help, but I’m a bit worried about the timing and where we’ll store everything. Do we have a clear plan for pickup and drop-off?

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Do we have that confirmed yet, or are we still figuring it out?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: We’re still figuring it out, I think. I’d feel better once we know the pickup time and where everything will go.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: I can help spread the word about the repair drive and connect folks who want to pitch in.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: That would be wonderful, Jules — thank you. I’ll let you know what folks need most so you can spread it around.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Absolutely — just send me the list, and I’ll pass it along to both groups I know.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I’ve got a note of what we have on hand, and I can check what still needs to be brought for the repair drive.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Thanks, Cleo — I’m usually running a bit late, but I can bring something if you tell me what’s still needed.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I’ll check the list and let you know what’s still missing so you can grab one of those. If you’re running late, I’ll keep it simple.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, the repair drive? I heard they’re hoping to get a good turnout this weekend—if you’ve got anything broken, now’s the time to bring it by.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: That’s perfect—I can swing by after school drop-off with a couple of things. Hopefully they can fix them up!

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, absolutely—just make sure to label each item if you can, and they’ll sort through the rest. I’m hoping they’ve got enough volunteers this time!

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Rosa, I’m in—just point me to what needs fixing and I’ll help where I can.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Thanks, Bo — that’s great to hear. I’ll send you the list of urgent fixes and we can start with the porch light and the loose fence panel.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Perfect, send it over and I’ll knock out the porch light first.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely — I’m happy to help with the repair drive. What do you need me to do?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Thanks, Sam — could you help sort the donations and load the boxes? I’ll handle the list and the drop-off.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely, Leo — I can sort the donations and help load the boxes. Just let me know where you want me to start.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: I’m putting together a little repair drive and would love for you to come by—there’ll be tools, snacks, and plenty of helping hands.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: That sounds really nice—thanks for inviting me. I’ll try to stop by and see what I can help with.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: That’d be great, Nell—I’d love to see you there. No pressure, just swing by whenever you can!

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I’ve got a clear note of the repair drive location if you need it—just tell me what part you want tracked.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Thanks, Opal. Just keep track of the location and any time it changes, and I’ll follow the plan from there.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Absolutely — I’ll keep the repair drive location noted and flag any changes as they come up.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Could you tell me what’s left to fix for the drive?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: I should check the list first so I don’t miss anything—give me a moment, and I’ll tell you what’s left.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Sure—take your time. Let me know what’s still on the list when you check it.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: I’ve been out running errands, and I heard the repair drive is picking up some good donations. What do you need me to keep an eye out for?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, thanks, Ira — if you spot any old hand tools, extension cords, or a sturdy ladder, those would be a big help. I’m a bit scattered today, so I appreciate you keeping watch.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: You got it—I’ll keep an eye out for hand tools, extension cords, and a sturdy ladder while I’m out.
